reuse.why: Fintegra uses the existing linking and bank-selection helpers, shares transaction downloading with Akahu, and reuses the unlink field definition.

duplication.why: The main linking and download decisions are shared, but fintegraAccounts duplicates the existing authenticated account-list request flow.

placement.why: Link policies remain in the shared account-link handler, transaction transport stays in sync.ts, and provider configuration and types follow existing layers.

scope.why: The changes largely support the requested rules and provider integration, although the additional account-list endpoint goes beyond the specified API.

maintainability.why: Centralized validation and unlink fields keep future policy changes manageable, with only minor additional account-list boilerplate.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All six provider link handlers use linkBankSyncAccount, and replacement shares unlinkedAccountFields with unlinkAccount.

disguised_duplication.where: The duplicated fintegraAccounts request flow is a direct provider-specific copy rather than reshaped or concealed logic.

abstraction_drift.where: linkBankSyncAccount adds replaceExistingLink and closed-target/conflicting-link rejection branches; downloadServerTransactions adds serverUrl and providerName parameters, while all linking consumers retain the shared path.
